Dettifoss and a row of waterfalls

Reynisfjara Beach: recent changes due to coastal erosion
Earth Lagoon Myvatn (formerly Myvatn Nature Baths)
Safetravel: eruptions and earthquakes in Reykjanes peninsula
Ground uplift and magma accumulation continue beneath Svartsengi (read through search results; the fetched page showed only the site banner)
Iceland route, stops and activity limits (research)

wikidata.note: confirmed by a person-run check (agent, 2026-10-18): 'hot springs in Iceland', 65.631 -16.848; a second item Q140586475 'Earth Lagoon Myvatn' has 1 sitelink and should be merged

draw.note: No own designation; the operator markets it as the north's lagoon. Visitors add it when staying at Myvatn, not a reason to come.

standing.note: The main geothermal bath of the Myvatn area.

records.standing_scope: North Iceland, Akureyri to Myvatn and Dettifoss

distinction.note: Same class within 100 km: GeoSea at Husavik (about 50 km) and the Forest Lagoon at Akureyri.

easy_payoff.note: the bath is the visit; there is no easier way

weather.note: A warm outdoor bath works in rain and wind.

records.why: A warm milky geothermal bath above Myvatn, a quieter alternative to the Blue Lagoon.

access_cost.note: nothing beyond the parking fees, which are not an access-cost type

designations.note: no designation named on the land manager's pages read

wikidata.note: confirmed by a person-run check (agent, 2026-10-18): 'volcanic system in Iceland' (Svartsengi), 63.878 -22.448; the record is the lava landscape around it

draw.note: No own designation on the pages read (Reykjanes is a UNESCO Global Geopark, a type our list lacks); a bonus stop beside the airport.

standing.note: Fresh lava is also at Fagradalsfjall and Eldhraun.

distinction.note: Same class within 100 km: Eldhraun, Fagradalsfjall and the Reykjanes lava fields.

easy_payoff.note: The lava fields are seen from the road.

weather.note: The landscape reads in any weather; views of the craters need clear air.

records.why: Young lava fields of the 2020s eruptions, seen on the drive from the airport.

access_cost.note: nothing beyond the parking fees, which are not an access-cost type

designations.note: no designation named on the land manager's pages read

wikidata.note: confirmed by a person-run check (agent, 2026-10-18): 'waterfall in Iceland', 64.703 -20.980

draw.note: Natural monument (own) since 1987; the land manager calls it among the most popular destinations in West Iceland.

standing.note: The best-known waterfalls of Borgarfjordur.

distinction.note: No other spring-fed falls seeping out of a lava field along a kilometre of cliff are known within 500 km.

records.unique_because: Spring water seeps from under a lava field in hundreds of falls along about 1 km of cliff.

easy_payoff.note: Viewpoints sit beside the car park, with partial wheelchair access (land manager).

weather.note: Waterfalls work in rain.

records.why: Clear springs pour out of a lava field into a glacial river, beside the Barnafoss arches.

access_cost.note: nothing beyond the parking fees, which are not an access-cost type

v.name: among the most popular tourist destinations in West Iceland

wikidata.note: confirmed by a person-run check (agent, 2026-10-18): 'waterfall', 65.822 -16.388

draw.note: Natural monument (own) since 1996; the national park's page leads with 'the most powerful waterfall in Europe' (official_highlight). Inside Vatnajokull National Park (parent).

standing.note: The headline waterfall of the north.

records.standing_scope: North Iceland, Akureyri to Myvatn and Dettifoss

distinction.note: Godafoss (about 70 km) is the other big northern fall; Selfoss and Hafragilsfoss are in the same canyon.

easy_payoff.note: A 1 km walk from the west car park gets the main view; part of the platform is shut after a landslide.

weather.note: Spray and power work in any weather.

records.why: Europe's most powerful waterfall, 44 m into the Jokulsargljufur canyon.

access_cost.note: nothing beyond the parking fees, which are not an access-cost type

v.name: the most powerful waterfall in Europe

wikidata.note: confirmed by a person-run check (agent, 2026-10-18): 'geyser in southwestern Iceland', 64.314 -20.299 (Great Geysir; Strokkur is Q1128186)

draw.note: Natural monument (own); the land manager calls it one of the most renowned hot spring areas in the world; a Golden Circle anchor.

standing.note: The geyser field of Iceland.

distinction.note: The geyser that named all geysers; no other erupting geyser in Iceland is regular like Strokkur.

records.unique_because: The place name Geysir gave the word geyser to many languages (land manager).

easy_payoff.note: Strokkur erupts beside the path from the car park.

weather.note: The eruptions do not depend on the weather.

records.why: Strokkur erupts every few minutes in the field that gave the word geyser.

access_cost.note: nothing beyond the parking fees, which are not an access-cost type

v.name: one of the most renowned hot spring areas in the world

pairs_with.reason: Gullfoss is about 10 km up the road: the Golden Circle pair

wikidata.note: confirmed by a person-run check (agent, 2026-10-18): 'museum and reconstructed farm in Skagafjordur', 65.611 -19.505

draw.note: No own designation on the museum's page; a stop on the road between Akureyri and the west.

standing.note: The best-kept turf farm on the Ring Road route.

distinction.note: Turf farms: Laufas (about 100 km) and Vidimyri church nearby.

easy_payoff.note: The farm is beside the car park.

weather.note: Most of the visit is inside the turf houses.

records.why: A turf farm you walk through room by room, as rural Iceland lived until the 20th century.

access_cost.note: nothing beyond the parking fees, which are not an access-cost type

designations.note: no designation named on the land manager's pages read

wikidata.note: confirmed by a person-run check (agent, 2026-10-18): 'waterfall in Iceland', 65.683 -17.550

draw.note: Natural monument (own) since 2020; the land manager calls it one of the largest waterfalls in Iceland by flow.

standing.note: The roadside waterfall of the north.

records.standing_scope: North Iceland, Akureyri to Myvatn and Dettifoss

distinction.note: Dettifoss (about 70 km) and Aldeyjarfoss in the same region.

easy_payoff.note: Right off Route 1 (plan).

weather.note: Waterfalls work in rain.

records.why: A wide horseshoe fall right on Route 1, with a saga story.

access_cost.note: nothing beyond the parking fees, which are not an access-cost type

wikidata.note: confirmed by a person-run check (agent, 2026-10-18): 'waterfall in Iceland', 64.326 -20.121

draw.note: Protected since 1979 (own); the land manager calls it one of Iceland's best known waterfalls; a Golden Circle anchor.

standing.note: The headline waterfall of the Golden Circle.

distinction.note: Big falls into canyons also at Dettifoss (far) and Haifoss; within 100 km it stands out.

easy_payoff.note: The upper viewpoint is by the car park (plan).

weather.note: Spray and power work in any weather.

records.why: A two-tier fall dropping into a canyon; the upper and lower views differ.

access_cost.note: nothing beyond the parking fees, which are not an access-cost type

v.name: one of Iceland's best known waterfalls

pairs_with.reason: Geysir is about 10 km back down the road: the Golden Circle pair

tried: Wikidata search 'Hverir' (Q2113293 has no description or coordinates, rejected)
Namafjall Q940545 is the mountain above, not the field

draw.note: No own designation found; visitors to Myvatn add it, but nobody plans Iceland around it.

standing.note: The most striking mud-pot field at Myvatn.

records.standing_scope: North Iceland, Akureyri to Myvatn and Dettifoss

distinction.note: Krafla's Viti and Leirhnjukur (about 10 km) and Geysir (far) are the comparable fields.

easy_payoff.note: The field is beside the car park.

weather.note: Steam shows best in cool damp air.

records.why: Boiling mud pots and steaming vents on bare orange ground below Namafjall.

access_cost.note: nothing beyond the parking fees, which are not an access-cost type

designations.note: no designation named on the land manager's pages read

pairs_with.reason: The lagoon is a few kilometres west on the same road at Myvatn: hot springs, then a soak

wikidata.note: confirmed by a person-run check (agent, 2026-10-18): 'waterfall in Iceland', 63.616 -19.993

draw.note: Place-level evidence: 40 Wikipedia languages (world) and about 22,400 English page views a year; no own designation page found (RC re-judge, 18 Oct 2026)

standing.note: The walk-behind waterfall of the south coast.

distinction.note: Gljufrabui is 500 m away; Skogafoss is 30 km away (same class).

records.unique_because: One of few big falls with a path all the way behind it.

easy_payoff.note: The front view is from the car park; the walk behind is the full payoff.

weather.note: You get wet anyway.

records.why: A 60 m curtain of water you can walk behind.

access_cost.note: nothing beyond the parking fees, which are not an access-cost type

designations.note: no designation named on the land manager's pages read

wikidata.note: confirmed by a person-run check (agent, 2026-10-18): 'waterfall on the Skoga River in Iceland', 63.530 -19.514

draw.note: Natural monument designation (own) since 1987, managed by the land manager with a ranger all year; one of the classic south-coast images.

standing.note: The biggest roadside fall of the south coast.

distinction.note: Seljalandsfoss is 30 km away; Kvernufoss is behind the museum.

easy_payoff.note: The base is by the car park.

weather.note: Spray and rainbows; works in rain.

records.why: A 60 m fall straight off the old sea cliff, with stairs to the top.

access_cost.note: nothing beyond the parking fees, which are not an access-cost type

wikidata.note: confirmed by a person-run check (agent, 2026-10-18): 'botanical garden in Akureyri, Iceland', 65.675 -18.093

draw.note: Protected public park by law, no other designation; a town outing for anyone staying in Akureyri.

standing.note: The best garden in the north; a rest-day stop.

distinction.note: Few botanic gardens in Iceland; Reykjavik's is 390 km away.

easy_payoff.note: Free, flat and step-free (garden).

weather.note: A garden is better in sun.

records.why: A free, step-free town garden of Arctic plants, with a cafe.

access_cost.note: nothing beyond the parking fees, which are not an access-cost type

wikidata.note: confirmed by a person-run check (agent, 2026-10-18): 'town in Iceland', 64.25 -15.217 (the record is its harbour)

draw.note: No designation; a base town for the glacier lagoons, not a reason to come.

standing.note: The langoustine town of the south-east.

distinction.note: Harbour towns all along the coast.

easy_payoff.note: The harbour is the town centre.

weather.note: A town works in any weather.

records.why: A working fishing harbour with views of Vatnajokull's outlet glaciers.

access_cost.note: nothing beyond the parking fees, which are not an access-cost type

designations.note: no designation named on the land manager's pages read

wikidata.note: confirmed by a person-run check (agent, 2026-10-18): 'harbour in Iceland', 64.153 -21.937

draw.note: No designation; part of any Reykjavik day, not a reason to come (no top list checked).

standing.note: The capital's harbour quarter.

distinction.note: Harbour quarters in every town.

easy_payoff.note: A walk from the centre.

weather.note: Museums and cafes for rain.

records.why: The capital's old harbour: boats, museums and cafes a short walk from the centre.

access_cost.note: nothing beyond the parking fees, which are not an access-cost type

designations.note: no designation named on the land manager's pages read

wikidata.note: confirmed by a person-run check (agent, 2026-10-18): 'town in Iceland', 65.260 -14.006 (not the fjord items Q2275965 and Q1641039)

draw.note: No designation found; the best-known town of the East Fjords and the ferry port, a detour for those in the east.

standing.note: The prettiest fjord town in the east.

distinction.note: Other East Fjords towns (Faskrudsfjordur, Djupivogur) within 100 km, none as known.

easy_payoff.note: The town is the visit.

weather.note: The pass and the fjord view need clear air.

records.why: A small fjord town of wooden houses, a rainbow street and the blue church.

access_cost.note: nothing beyond the parking fees, which are not an access-cost type

designations.note: no designation named on the land manager's pages read

tried: Wikidata search 'Hellnar' (Q1366915 is the village); no item for the path

draw.note: The coast is protected (1979) and inside Snaefellsjokull National Park (parent); a highlight of a Snaefellsnes day, not of a trip.

standing.note: The classic short coastal walk of Snaefellsnes.

distinction.note: Basalt sea-cliff walks also at Londrangar and Svalthufa (about 10 km).

easy_payoff.note: The arches and cliffs at Arnarstapi are beside the car park.

weather.note: Cliffs and birds need dry weather; it works in cloud.

records.why: A 2 km coastal path over lava past sea arches, bird cliffs and the old fishing village.

access_cost.note: nothing beyond the parking fees, which are not an access-cost type

wikidata.note: confirmed by a person-run check (agent, 2026-10-18): 'bay in Iceland', 64.752 -23.901

draw.note: Inside Snaefellsjokull National Park (parent); a highlight of a Snaefellsnes day.

standing.note: The best beach stop on the peninsula.

distinction.note: Black beaches elsewhere on Snaefellsnes and the south coast; the lifting stones and the 1948 wreck are its own.

easy_payoff.note: The wheelchair-accessible platform gives the view; the beach is down a lava path.

weather.note: A storm beach works in rough weather from a safe distance.

records.why: A black pebble beach with an old trawler wreck and four fishermen's lifting stones.

access_cost.note: nothing beyond the parking fees, which are not an access-cost type

wikidata.note: confirmed by a person-run check (agent, 2026-10-18): 'valley in Iceland', 63.771 -18.172

draw.note: Place-level evidence: 17 Wikipedia languages and about 7,700 page views a year (national by languages); the land manager (Environment Agency) closed it in 2019 because of visitor pressure (repo research); no own designation page read (RC re-judge, 18 Oct 2026)

standing.note: The south coast's canyon walk.

distinction.note: Mulagljufur and Stakkholtsgja are comparable canyons within about 100 km.

easy_payoff.note: The first viewpoints are close to the lower car park (plan).

weather.note: The moss and depth read better in sun, fine in cloud.

records.why: A 100 m deep mossy canyon seen from a rim path with platforms.

access_cost.note: nothing beyond the parking fees, which are not an access-cost type

designations.note: no designation named on the land manager's pages read

wikidata.note: confirmed by a person-run check (agent, 2026-10-18): 'waterfall surrounded with basalt columns in Iceland', 64.028 -16.975

draw.note: The national park calls Svartifoss one of the highlights of Skaftafell; inside Vatnajokull National Park (parent).

standing.note: The classic Skaftafell walk.

distinction.note: Basalt-column falls also at Aldeyjarfoss and Hengifoss, both far.

easy_payoff.note: The marked S2 loop (5.8 km, 'Easy') reaches the falls; the longer circuits add views, not the falls.

weather.note: A forest walk to a waterfall works in rain.

records.why: A waterfall framed by black basalt columns, on a marked loop from the visitor centre.

access_cost.note: nothing beyond the parking fees, which are not an access-cost type

v.name: one of the highlights of Skaftafell

wikidata.note: confirmed by a person-run check (agent, 2026-10-18): 'canyon in Iceland' (Almannagja), 64.261 -21.122; the park is Q107370

draw.note: Inside Thingvellir National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage site (parent); the Assembly site is the park's most visited location (land manager).

standing.note: The rift walk of the Golden Circle.

distinction.note: Nowhere else can you walk down a continental rift to the site of a 10th-century parliament.

records.unique_because: A walkable continental rift that is also the site of the parliament founded in 930.

easy_payoff.note: The walk down Almannagja from the Hakid visitor centre is the visit.

weather.note: A gorge walk works in rain.

records.why: Walk down the rift between two plates to where the Althing met from 930.

access_cost.note: nothing beyond the parking fees, which are not an access-cost type

v.name: the national park's most visited location, the Assembly Haven

wikidata.note: confirmed by a person-run check (agent, 2026-10-18): 'Diamond Beach', 64.053 -16.153 in Iceland (not the Australian, US or Ontario items)

draw.note: Down a tier: the earlier national rested on the parent designation (Vatnajokull National Park, scope parent); no Wikipedia article (0 languages). It is the lagoon's beach across the road, and the lagoon carries the draw (RC re-judge, 18 Oct 2026)

standing.note: The iceberg beach.

distinction.note: Fjallsarlon's shore (10 km) has ice but no surf beach; nothing else like it in the country.

easy_payoff.note: The beach is beside the Fellsfjara car parks.

weather.note: Depends on what ice has washed up; better in low sun.

records.why: Lagoon icebergs washed onto black sand; whatever the sea left that day.

access_cost.note: nothing beyond the parking fees, which are not an access-cost type

pairs_with.reason: The lagoon is across the road; the beach's ice comes from it

wikidata.note: confirmed by a person-run check (agent, 2026-10-18): 'glacial lake', 64.070 -16.212

draw.note: The national park calls the lagoons among the most popular tourist destinations in the country; inside Vatnajokull National Park (parent).

standing.note: The glacier lagoon of Iceland.

distinction.note: Fjallsarlon (about 10 km) is the same class, smaller.

easy_payoff.note: The shore is beside the car park.

weather.note: Icebergs show in any light; the glacier view needs clear air.

records.why: Icebergs calving from Breidamerkurjokull drift in a lagoon beside the Ring Road.

access_cost.note: nothing beyond the parking fees, which are not an access-cost type

v.name: among the most popular tourist destinations in the country

pairs_with.reason: Diamond Beach is across the road from the lagoon, where its icebergs wash up

wikidata.note: confirmed by a person-run check (agent, 2026-10-18): 'mountain in Snaefellsnes peninsula', 64.948 -23.311 (Kirkjufellsfoss is Q2447177)

draw.note: Place-level evidence: 22 Wikipedia languages and about 25,400 English page views a year (national); no designation or top list, so not world (RC re-judge, 18 Oct 2026)

standing.note: The classic view of Snaefellsnes.

distinction.note: Vestrahorn at Stokksnes is the other famous mountain view (far).

easy_payoff.note: The view with the waterfall is a short walk from the car park.

weather.note: The peak needs clear air; it hides in low cloud.

records.why: The cone-shaped mountain above Kirkjufellsfoss, Iceland's best-known mountain view.

access_cost.note: nothing beyond the parking fees, which are not an access-cost type

designations.note: no designation named on the land manager's pages read

wikidata.note: confirmed by a person-run check (agent, 2026-10-18): 'black sand beach in southern Iceland near ... Vik', 63.405 -19.064

draw.note: The Tourist Board calls it a very popular tourist destination (headline) and one of the most dangerous; a south-coast anchor.

standing.note: The black-sand beach of the south coast.

distinction.note: Black beaches at Dyrholaey (5 km) and Solheimasandur; the basalt columns and stacks are its own.

easy_payoff.note: Since February 2026 only the upper ridge is reachable; the basalt columns are off limits.

weather.note: Dramatic in storms, but the zones close the lower beach.

records.why: Black sand, basalt columns and the Reynisdrangar stacks, seen from the upper ridge.

access_cost.note: nothing beyond the parking fees, which are not an access-cost type

v.name: a very popular tourist destination (Icelandic Tourist Board)

wikidata.note: confirmed by a person-run check (agent, 2026-10-18): 'mountain in Iceland', 64.807 -23.776 (the park is Q738103)

draw.note: Inside Snaefellsjokull National Park (parent); a view, not a destination, on a Snaefellsnes day.

standing.note: The glacier is seen from many points on the peninsula.

distinction.note: The glacier is visible from much of the peninsula.

easy_payoff.note: A roadside view.

weather.note: The glacier cap is often in cloud; without clear air there is nothing to see.

records.why: The glacier-capped volcano Jules Verne made the entrance to the centre of the earth.
